findings.title: Release the map guard before running the held-lock body
findings.comment: The `yield` remains inside `async with self._guard`, so the global guard is held throughout the caller's computation. Consequently, `JobQueue` workers computing different keys serialize behind one another, and a stalled handler blocks all other cache misses. A factory that computes another key through the same cache also deadlocks. Keep the guard scoped to reference-map updates and run lock acquisition and the caller's body outside it.

findings.title: Clear and signal in-flight computations on every exit
findings.comment: If `factory()` raises or is cancelled, execution skips both removal of the in-flight entry and signaling its event. Existing waiters and every later request for that key then wait forever. This also breaks the default retry path: a handler that fails once hangs on its second attempt without being called again, so `drain()` and shutdown cannot finish. Put event cleanup and signaling in a `finally` block covering the computation.

findings.title: Check expiry before extending a hot entry's deadline
findings.comment: Once an entry has enough hits—or an expired read brings it to the threshold—this code replaces its deadline before checking whether it has already expired. A read after an arbitrarily long idle period therefore revives and serves the old value instead of recomputing it. An injected-clock check confirmed that a previously hot entry remained unchanged long after its deadline. Check the original deadline before counting the read or sliding expiry.

findings.title: Keep cache counter names aligned with the hit-rate reader
findings.comment: The cache now emits `cache.get.hit`, `cache.get.hit_after_wait`, and `cache.get.miss`, but `JobQueue.cache_hit_rate()` still reads their old names. With the default shared counters, its total consequently stays zero and it reports a hit rate of 1.0 regardless of actual traffic. This also makes `warm_stale_keys()` always skip its work; a check with one observed miss reported 1.0 and refreshed no keys. Update the reader together with the renamed counters, or retain the existing names.

findings.title: Apply the waiting timeout to in-flight joins
findings.comment: When another computation already owns the key, this unbounded event wait bypasses both the per-call `timeout` and the configured `lock_timeout`, which are only applied later to lock acquisition. Thus the same-key contention these options are meant to bound can still hold a caller indefinitely. A waiter with a 10 ms timeout remained pending beyond 30 ms while its producer was running. Resolve the effective timeout before this branch and apply it to the event wait as well.

explanation: incorrect — Targeted checks reproduced serialization of unrelated keys, hung retries, stale-value resurrection, ignored join timeouts, and disabled warm-up after an observed cache miss. These regressions affect the cache and worker pool's documented behavior; the working tree was left unchanged.
